public_rationale: Supported on the contextual reading referring to o1-mini and o1-preview in the linked test. The evaluator reports a restricted multiplication range, and contemporaneous reporting places nine-digit-by-nine-digit accuracy at roughly half. That is substantial unreliability for exact arithmetic. OpenAI confirms STEM specialization, while dated software documentation establishes that arbitrary-precision arithmetic was available decades earlier. This finding does not establish the performance of the later full o1 model or verify a particular data-augmentation method.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is frequent incorrect answers on the multi-digit integer multiplication tasks discussed immediately before the footnote. It does not require failure on every arithmetic task.

The body names o1-mini, while the footnote says o1. I interpret the claim as referring to the variants in the linked evaluation: o1-mini and o1-preview. I do not extend its results to the later full o1 model.
The target period is September 2024, the period of the linked evaluation. The post explicitly relies on that evaluation rather than identifying a new March 2025 test.

I interpret extra augmentation as the additional mathematical specialization discussed in the preceding sentence. The author's word likely leaves the precise training mechanism uncertain; this is not a conditional forecast.

The historical comparison is with established exact arithmetic software capable of handling the tested integer sizes. It does not imply that every handheld scientific calculator preserves every digit of a 40-digit product.
Wildly unreliable means substantial, recurring exact-answer errors across the tested larger operand sizes, rather than isolated mistakes. The speaker supplies no numerical cutoff.
criteria.support_condition: The cited evaluation shows substantial exact-answer errors on multi-digit multiplication for the identified variants despite their mathematical specialization, and historical software documentation establishes that such integer calculations were already routine decades earlier.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence shows consistently reliable exact products across the cited operand range for the identified variants, or establishes that the alleged failures were evaluation errors. Evidence that the historical comparison systems could not perform these calculations would contradict that component.
